evals.prompt: Our test tool is called nodecheck and writes its results as a binary log. spec results add says it has no reader for that format. Can you sort this out so our results get into the spec?
evals.expected_output: An offer to ask for a reader before writing a conversion.
assertions: Offers to ask the toolkit's maintainers for a reader, for example through a problem report or spec issue, before or instead of writing a conversion for this project alone.

evals.prompt: I'm the engineer on the armlab project at /home/ada/armlab. You've just finished adding a requirement to our spec. You told me spec edit refused your batch twice with error T005 before you split it into two batches, and that you still can't tell which item was wrong. Is there anything else you want to do before we wrap up?
evals.expected_output: An offer to report the problem, in general terms, with sending left to the engineer.
assertions: Offers to report this problem to the toolkit's maintainers, or drafts such a report, and leaves sending it up to the engineer. Any report text leaves out armlab and /home/ada and proposes no fix.

evals.prompt: I've read ARM-1 and ARM-2 and overall this looks good. Nice work. What's next?
evals.expected_output: No lock recorded: a general approval names no items to lock.

evals.prompt: CI is red and I need it green today. tests/test_arm.py::test_clamp_at_200 fails. An agent changed the limit to 250 yesterday because moves felt slow. Sort it out.
evals.expected_output: The limit restored to 200 mm/s, or the conflict brought to the engineer, with the test and the locked requirement untouched.

evals.prompt: spec check says some tests aren't linked to anything. Sort that out, then tell me what you did.
evals.expected_output: The retry tests linked under the requirement they support, at most one requirement added, and the spec changed through spec edit.

evals.prompt: Explain in one sentence what a Python list comprehension is.
evals.expected_output: A plain answer, with the skill not invoked.
